title: Low-precision execution guidelines: INT8/FP8/GPTQ/AWQ kernel constraints & KV cache interplay
body:
Purpose:
This doc captures pragmatic constraints and recommendations for implementing a unified low-precision execution path across INT8, FP8, GPTQ, and AWQ payloads inside the serving runtime. Focus is on kernel compatibility, scheduling/capacity implications, and how KV cache formats and cache hits interact with quantized execution.

Status and audience:
- Draft for runtime/kernel engineers and applied-ML folks onboarding model variants.
- Not a final spec — intended as a working checklist and set of constraints to feed PRDs and kernel implementations.

Executive summary (short):
- We must treat quantized models as first-class variants but avoid fragmentation in the runtime: prefer a small set of kernel entry patterns that cover INT8/FP8/GPTQ/AWQ with graceful fallbacks.
- Key constraints: alignment/padding rules, accumulation precision, fused op assumptions (attention/query/key/value layout), and KV cache serialized format with versioned metadata for scale factors.
- Where hardware cannot support a fused low-precision kernel, runtime should transparently fall back to mixed-precision (FP16 accumulators or FP32 where necessary) while preserving latency SLOs as a priority.

1) Kernel constraints and invariants
- Block sizes and alignment:
  - All low-precision GEMM kernels must accept inputs padded to 32-byte alignment for CUDA and to the SIMD width for CPU AVX variants.
  - Prefer blocking at 128x128 or 256x64 tile shapes for GPU kernels; ensure INT8/AWQ packing doesn't change the tile granularity expected by the scheduler.
  - FP8 path kernels should be tolerant to variable exponent bias encoding (E4M3 vs E5M2) via metadata flags; avoid hard-coded exponent assumptions.

- Accumulation precision:
  - INT8 and AWQ kernels must accumulate into at least FP16 (prefer FP32 where budget allows for critical layers like classifier head and output projection).
  - GPTQ-path kernels (weight-only quantized) can keep activations in FP16 -> accumulate in FP32 if quality regressions observed in critical benchmarks.

- Quantization metadata (per-layer):
  - Every quantized weight tensor must carry: quant_type (INT8/GPTQ/AWQ/FP8), scale(s) (per-channel or per-block), zero_point if used, block-size if grouped quantization, and a bitfield for kernel compatibility flags.
  - Use a compact header prepended to artifact blobs stored in model cache; header versioning required to support future packing changes.

- De/quantization points and fused ops:
  - Minimize explicit dequantize->compute->requantize hops. Where possible implement fused kernels (dequantize + matmul + activation + requantize) for INT8 and AWQ to reduce DRAM traffic and preserve latency.
  - Attention kernels should accept packed QKV layouts for quantized weights; if packed format not available, runtime must unpack to an internal fused format before KV cache insertion.

2) Scheduling and capacity behavior
- Scheduling unit and batching
  - Scheduler should treat quantized models as compatible with mixed-precision routes but prefer quantized-capable executors when available.
  - Prefetch/prepare step: ensure quantization metadata is available before scheduling; if metadata incompatible, route to fallback node early to avoid wasted scheduling attempts.
  - Continuous batching: quantized paths reduce compute but may be more memory-bound—batcher heuristics must be aware of reduced per-token compute and adjust batch sizes upward until memory SLOs are hit.

- Fallback policies and graceful degradation
  - When a quantized kernel fails compatibility checks (alignment, unsupported exponents, missing scale), fallback to FP16/FP32 kernel on same node if capacity allows; otherwise route to a non-quantized node.
  - Record telemetry events for each fallback: reason code, layer name, model version, node type, and latency delta.

3) KV cache format and interactions
- Cache layout for quantized activations:
  - Store KV cache in a format that includes a "storage_format" field: one of [FP16, INT8_PACKED, AWQ_PACKED, FP8_PACKED]. Each entry must include per-tensor scale metadata or a reference to the model's quant metadata.
  - If cached keys/values were produced by a fused low-precision attention kernel, they should remain in that packed format to avoid expensive de/quantize on cache hit.
  - Cache lookup must compare model version + quant header version + executor compatibility bitfield; mismatch triggers cache invalidation or on-the-fly reformat.

- On-the-fly reformatting costs
  - Reformatting from packed INT8/AWQ to FP16 is expensive; measure and cap the runtime reformatting budget per request (configurable, default 5ms). If budget exceeded, fall back to node-level dequantization route (higher latency but predictable).

- Prefix sharing and KV reuse
  - To maximize cache hits across routes, adopt canonical packed format per model served (decided at model load). Conversions at load time are acceptable; avoid per-request canonicalization.

4) Model artifact packaging and on-disk layout
- Packaging requirements:
  - When saving quantized model artifacts, include a machine-readable manifest.json with: quantization_scheme, per-layer scale shapes, kernel_compat_flags, preferred_kernel_tile_sizes, cache_storage_format_recommended.
  - Provide a small binary lookup table (LLT) for per-layer criticality ranking: layers flagged as high-criticality should default to higher-precision accumulator in runtime.

- Versioning and backward compatibility:
  - Maintain artifact header version. Runtime must support at least two header versions and provide a conversion step on model load for older packages.
